mission.title: Strong authentication and privileged access — Keycloak
mission.lead_auditor: Attest CI (automated run, no human auditor)
scope_in: Security settings of the Keycloak realm (password, lockout, session, logging)
Realm accounts and members of the admin role
scope_out: Intrinsic strength of MFA factors and custom authentication flows
Clients, identity federation and connected applications
Hosting and operation of the Keycloak server

target_label: Keycloak (open-source identity provider), through the read-only gateway

control.title: MFA enforced for privileged administrator accounts
control.objective: Every account holding the realm role admin must have multi-factor authentication configured.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve all members of the realm role admin via GET /api/kc/roles/admin/users and verify totp is true for each account.
control.expected: totp=true for all users with role admin
control.risk: Compromise of a password-only administrator account would allow full takeover of the identity provider.
control.recommendation: Enforce OTP enrollment for all admin accounts and remove privileged access until MFA is configured.
control.cause: MFA enrollment for administrators was not enforced at provisioning due to missing configuration or control.

before.expected: totp=true for all users with role admin

inspection.comment: Screenshot shows y.tanguy holding admin role with MFA marked no, matching the failed test.

control.title: MFA enforced for users of critical system
control.objective: Every user account in the Keycloak realm, which supports critical or important functions, must have multi-factor authentication configured.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve all user accounts via GET /api/kc/users with pagination and verify totp is true for each account.
control.risk: Password-only authentication exposes critical-function accounts to phishing and credential theft.
control.recommendation: Require OTP enrollment for all realm users and disable accounts that have not enrolled.
control.cause: MFA was not made mandatory by default for all users due to incomplete authentication flow configuration.

inspection.comment: Screenshot shows accounts 101-180 with y.tanguy as the only account with MFA marked no.

control.title: Minimum password length and complexity
control.objective: Password policy must require at least 12 characters with complexity requirements.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve the realm representation via GET /api/kc/realm and verify the passwordPolicy requires length 12 and complexity.
control.expected: passwordPolicy contains length(12) and upperCase, lowerCase, digits, specialChars
control.risk: Weak passwords can be brute-forced or guessed, leading to unauthorized access.
control.recommendation: Set the realm password policy to at least 12 characters with upper/lower case, digits and special characters.
control.cause: Secure password policy defaults were not applied when the realm was configured.

before.expected: passwordPolicy contains length(12) and upperCase, lowerCase, digits, specialChars
before.detail: Checked 1 realm representation and passwordPolicy does not require length 12 with upperCase, lowerCase, digits and specialChars.

inspection.comment: Screenshot shows passwordPolicy is length(14) with no complexity requirements.

control.title: Account lockout after repeated failures
control.objective: Account lockout must be enabled and trigger after at most 5 failed logins, never disabled.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve the realm representation via GET /api/kc/realm and verify bruteForceProtected is enabled with failureFactor at most 5.
control.risk: Without lockout, attackers can perform unlimited online password guessing against accounts.
control.recommendation: Enable brute-force protection and set the failure threshold to 5 attempts or fewer.
control.cause: Brute-force protection was left disabled or set too permissively during realm hardening.

before.detail: Realm has brute-force protection enabled with failureFactor 3.

inspection.comment: Screenshot shows bruteForceProtected True and failureFactor 3, matching the automated pass result.

control.title: Inactive session timeout
control.objective: Idle sessions must expire after at most 15 minutes and idle timeout must never be disabled.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve the realm representation via GET /api/kc/realm and verify ssoSessionIdleTimeout is set to 900 seconds or less.
control.risk: Overly long idle sessions allow session hijacking from unattended workstations.
control.recommendation: Set the SSO idle session timeout to 15 minutes or less.
control.cause: Session timeout was left at the insecure default value due to missing hardening baseline.

inspection.comment: The screenshot shows ssoSessionIdleTimeout is 1800 seconds, exceeding the 900-second limit.

control.title: Logging of administration actions
control.objective: All administration actions must be recorded as admin events.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve the realm representation via GET /api/kc/realm and verify adminEventsEnabled is true.
control.risk: Without admin audit logging, malicious or erroneous privileged changes cannot be detected or investigated.
control.recommendation: Enable admin events recording for the realm including details and secure retention.
control.cause: Audit event collection was not enabled as part of the logging baseline for the realm.

before.detail: Realm representation shows adminEventsEnabled is True.

inspection.comment: Screenshot shows adminEventsEnabled is True matching the expected value.

control.title: No generic or shared administrator accounts
control.objective: No account holding the realm role admin may be generic or shared, each admin must have a nominative username of form initiale.nom and a personal email, not a function identifier or shared mailbox.
control.test_procedure: Retrieve all members of the realm role admin via GET /api/kc/roles/admin/users and verify username and email are nominative and not generic or shared.
control.expected: for role admin members, username matches initiale.nom pattern and email is personal, no generic username (ops, admin, root) or shared mailbox (ops-partage@, admin@)
control.risk: Shared administrator accounts prevent accountability and allow uncontrolled privileged access.
control.recommendation: Remove admin rights from all generic or shared accounts and reissue nominative administrator accounts.
control.cause: Use of operational shared accounts for administration persisted due to missing joiner-mover-leaver and naming controls.

before.expected: for role admin members, username matches initiale.nom pattern and email is personal, no generic username (ops, admin, root) or shared mailbox (ops-partage@, admin@)
before.detail: Checked 4 admin members, all have nominative initiale.nom username and personal email.

inspection.field_text: a.bihan armelle.bihan@menhir-finance.example admin yes yes; l.guivarch loic.guivarch@menhir-finance.example admin yes yes; m.pichon maiwenn.pichon@menhir-finance.example admin yes yes; y.tanguy yannick.tanguy@menhir-finance.example admin yes no
inspection.comment: The screenshot lists four admin accounts all with initiale.nom usernames and personal emails.
